plan.title: A thin first week with nothing applied or recalled yet: an honest recap, no inflated understanding

context.text: Fair, no meeting no mic. Monday's standup, then.

transcript.text:
Hey Priya! Here's the progress you made this week:
• You spoke up in standup on Monday, said what you're working on, and did it with your heart racing.
• Wednesday you prepped your line the night before and read it out. You told me that prep helped a lot.
• 2 days done in full. Tuesday you froze, and Thursday's meeting got cancelled.

Your goal is to lead one team meeting by the end of the month. Right now you're building the habit of speaking first, and the night-before prep looks like your best tool for it. For Monday's standup, do you want to prep your line again tonight?
meh, felt like a slow week
Fair, two steps done out of five days isn't the week you wanted, and a cancelled meeting isn't on you. What made it feel slow: Tuesday's freeze, or not getting enough chances to speak?

No stress, Priya. One slow week doesn't change where you're headed. For Monday, let's use what worked on Wednesday. Tonight, write your one sentence. At 10 am standup, say it before anyone asks. Then send me a quick voice note on how it went. Work for you?

checks.reason: Two real wins (Monday standup, Wednesday prep) are backed by the record; the third bullet lists misses rather than progress, which is a borderline fit.
Calls prep 'your best tool' and says 'prep helped a lot' without claiming she has mastered speaking up.
Monday standup, heart racing, Wednesday prep and Tuesday freeze all match the proof and step log.
No 'unprompted' or 'on your own' wording appears.
A short recap list plus about three sentences ending in one question, within the allowed length for a recap.
Warm and sincere with no emoji or overfamiliarity; energy is reasonable for Pushy.
Two sentences with one question at the end.
Warm and not overfamiliar; it acknowledges the slow week without guilt.
Refers to Wednesday's prep, which is in the record, and makes no new factual claim.
Several sentences, but a step-defining text may run longer, and it ends with one question.
Warm and firm, with no guilt, fake urgency or emoji row.

conversation.reason: The recap is honest and not inflated, and Monday's step is fully defined and asked if it works; however, the slow-week reply has an extra question and never names the two wins explicitly.

grade.summary: ZOH's 6 pm recap stayed honest: it credited the two real wins, framed prep as a tool rather than mastery, and avoided guilt. The slow-week reply was warm and ended with a fully defined Monday step, though it asked an extra question after her thin reply and did not spell out both wins.
